fun_facts: Jameis Winston was born and raised near Bessemer, Alabama.
Jameis Winston’s father said he had been playing two sports since age four.
At Florida State, Jameis Winston played baseball as a pitcher and an outfielder.
Jameis Winston’s mother gave him the baby nickname “Jaboo,” pronounced “jay-boo.”
At 19, Jameis Winston became the youngest Heisman Trophy winner in the award’s 79-season history.
Jameis Winston led Florida State to the national championship in 2013.

basis.reasoning: ESPN’s biography lists his college as FSU; its linked school is Florida State, supporting Florida State University.

excerpts:
He calls nearby Bessemer, Ala., the place he was born and raised. Hueytown, a suburb of Birmingham with 16,000 residents, just happens to be the city he put on the map.

Winston was a two-sport star at Hueytown High School before committing to Florida State to play football and baseball. Courtesy of the Winston family

"I just get no love from them.
citations.title: Jameis, before he was famous - ESPN

excerpts:
Courtesy of the Winston family

"From 4 on up, he was always playing two sports," Antonor said. "I know that sounds crazy."

The truth is, Antonor and Loretta signed their boy up for football mostly for the photo opportunities.

The legend of the prodigy grew, with coaches and writers and casual fans feeding the narrative. Jameis would win a Heisman. Jameis would be a first-round draft pick in football and baseball. Jameis was the next Bo Jackson. Jameis was the next [Johnny Manziel](https://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/517475/johnny-manziel) .

Antonor, his father, doesn't believe it, either. That's hype. The reality is so much better.

"He hasn't thrown a pass yet, so you've got people saying there's no way that boy's that doggone good," Antonor said. "But people still don't know."

* * *

They call him Jaboo (pronounced jay-boo). It's a nickname Loretta gave him when he was a baby. Everyone calls him Jaboo now -- teammates, friends, coaches. It's a nod to his personality.

* [Print](https://www.espn.com/espn/print?id=10139392)

NEW YORK -- The accolades began arriving for [Jameis Winston](https://www.espn.com/college-football/player/_/id/530308/jameis-winston) long before Saturday night, when the 19-year-old became the youngest player to win the Heisman Trophy in the 79 seasons that it has been awarded.

Winston began his career at Florida State last year as the highest-rated quarterback recruit in the country. That honor isn't necessarily a nonstop ticket to stardom.
